clue.text: A boxer good at putting up a guard?

definitions.text: A boxer good at putting up a guard?

parts.words: A boxer good at putting up a guard?
parts.note: a boxer here is the breed of dog, not a fighter, and the guard it puts up is keeping watch over a house

explanation.surface: A pugilist praised for keeping his defensive stance high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' and 'guard' both pull towards the boxing ring; the boxer is a dog breed and a guard dog keeps watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog kept to protect property and raise the alarm is the literal sense of the word.

clue.text: Bond needed in companies' crowdfunding

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of letters across the words companies' crowdfunding

explanation.surface: A financial bond is required when firms raise money through crowdfunding.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the gap: compani-ES CROW-dfunding.
explanation.definitionFit: An escrow is a deed or bond held by a third party until a condition is met.

clue.text: Fast runner — he holds a record at first

indicators.note: the word he grips the other letters between its two letters, as if holding them

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the opening letter of record is wanted

explanation.surface: A speedy athlete who holds a record from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts A and R (first of 'record') between H and E.
explanation.definitionFit: The hare is the animal proverbial for its speed, as in the tortoise and the hare.

clue.text: Karate instructor is seen getting beaten up

indicators.note: being beaten up leaves the letters of is seen battered into a new order

explanation.surface: A martial arts teacher is spotted being assaulted.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensei is the Japanese title for a teacher or master of a martial art.

clue.text: Salvage works outside small desert city

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the letter for small
to work something is to knead or reshape it, so the letters of Salvage are reshaped

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Salvage operations go on beyond a small town in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' signals the anagram and 'outside' puts the reworked letters around S; 'small desert city' reads as a single phrase, but 'small' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Las Vegas is the Nevada gambling city built in the Mojave Desert.

clue.text: Intolerant people try to get involved in scraps

indicators.note: the word for try becomes involved in, that is placed inside, the word for scraps

parts.note: scraps are bits
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: Bigoted folk try to get mixed up in fights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scraps' reads as fights but means leftover pieces; 'to get involved in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigot is someone who is prejudiced and will not accept other views.

clue.text: Sport: tired, endlessly

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the synonym for tired is dropped

parts.note: tired means weary

explanation.surface: A terse note on sport and exhaustion that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' is a verb here: to sport a hat is to wear it.
explanation.definitionFit: To sport clothing or an item is to have it on show on the body.

clue.text: Where Joan of Arc died is in question

definitions.meaning: she was burnt tied to a post, in 1431 at Rouen
something under discussion or at risk

explanation.surface: A historical fact about the French heroine is under debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Joan of Arc was burnt on a pyre post; an issue that is being decided or put at risk is likewise the phrase.

clue.text: Japanese cartoon featuring in seminars from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left
the answer features inside the letters of seminars

explanation.surface: A Japanese animation is shown in seminars originating in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featuring in' finds EMINA inside sEMINArs; 'from the east' reads it right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Anime is the Japanese style of animated film and television.

clue.text: Vet tailed by vehicle is cut up

indicators.note: placed beside: the vehicle comes next to the shortened vet

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: to tail a word here is to cut off its tail, its last letter

explanation.surface: A vet is followed by a car and is badly injured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailed' looks like 'followed' but means docked of its last letter; 'by' just places the vehicle beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve is to slice meat or wood into pieces.

clue.text: Various different means of being delivered

indicators.note: made different, so the letters of Various are rearranged

explanation.surface: There are many different ways of making a delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivered' suggests post, but here it is rescue: being delivered from evil.
explanation.definitionFit: A saviour is one who rescues, so is the agent of deliverance.

clue.text: Slump, depressed, next to item in playground

indicators.note: the two parts sit side by side

parts.note: depressed means down
a swing is playground equipment

explanation.surface: Someone slumps, feeling low, beside the playground equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A downswing is a downward trend, such as a fall in trade.

clue.text: Crooner pens a line for an American author

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the singer word encloses the other letters

parts.note: a crooner is a singer

explanation.surface: A crooner writes a line for a writer from the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pens' reads as writes but means encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: J D Salinger wrote The Catcher in the Rye.

clue.text: Very soft bread dipped in gravy?

parts.note: very means so, as in so tired
P is piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: Describing a piece of bread that has gone soggy in gravy.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: gravy is just one liquid bread might soak in.
explanation.definitionFit: A sop is a piece of bread soaked in liquid such as soup or gravy.

clue.text: Work on the top of a bottle to get port

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next part

parts.note: to ply a trade is to work at it
the opening at the top of a bottle is its mouth

explanation.surface: Working on a bottle top to get to the fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' wants to be the drink; it is the Devon harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Plymouth is a naval port city in Devon, in south-west England.

clue.text: It's painful parking after fitness centre closes early

indicators.note: the parking letter comes after the shortened word
the word stops before its final letter, as a shop closing early

parts.note: a gym is a fitness centre
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: Parking is a pain when the gym shuts early.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyp is informal British for pain, as in a bad back giving you gyp.

clue.text: Crime of passion is initially risqué

indicators.note: only the first letters of passion and is are taken

parts.note: risqué means racy

explanation.surface: A crime of passion begins as something saucy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crime of passion' reads as one phrase; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Piracy is robbery at sea, or illegal copying, both offences.

clue.text: Biography of Fry mixed up with Eliot's

indicators.note: the letters of the two names are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A biography of Stephen Fry gets confused with one of T S Eliot.
explanation.definitionFit: A biography is the account of a person's whole career from birth.

clue.text: A long time mostly producing fodder

indicators.note: most of the phrase is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: for ages means a long time

explanation.surface: Animal feed that takes a very long time to produce.
explanation.definitionFit: Forage is food for horses and cattle, such as hay.

clue.text: Awards zero marks

parts.note: O resembles the digit zero
scars are marks on the skin

explanation.surface: Prizes are given out with no marks at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscars are the Academy Awards for film.

clue.text: Sailor originally rowed into state by river

indicators.note: placed beside: the river letter goes next
that letter goes inside the name of the state

parts.note: Maine is a US state

indicators.note: only the first letter of rowed is wanted

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A sailor first rowed into a US state along a river.
explanation.walkthrough: R (first of 'rowed') goes into MAINE, then the river's R is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariner is a seaman, as in The Rime of the Ancient Mariner.

clue.text: Whisky and mead oddly left at the end of banquet

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of mead are taken, first and third
only the final letter of banquet is wanted

explanation.surface: Whisky and mead, strangely, are left over after a feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' gives MA from mead, the odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A malt is a single-malt Scotch, made from malted barley.

clue.text: North American company importing hot food from Mexico

indicators.note: the company letters take the hot letter inside, as goods are imported

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A US firm imports spicy Mexican food.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip topped with cheese, a Tex-Mex snack.

clue.text: In the first instance, niceties usually feel fairly sufficient

indicators.note: the first letters of the four following words are taken

explanation.surface: Pleasantries usually feel quite adequate at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuff is a colloquial clipping of enough, as in nuff said.

clue.text: Charlie smuggled by decoy for ill-gotten gains

indicators.note: the letter is carried in secretly, hidden inside the decoy word

parts.note: a lure is a decoy
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A drug dealer called Charlie is smuggled by a decoy for profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre, as in filthy lucre, is money gained dishonestly.

clue.text: When shattered, I forgot to strive for success

indicators.note: broken into pieces, so the letters of I forgot are reassembled

explanation.surface: Exhausted, I forgot to aim for success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattered' reads as exhausted but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Go for it is an exhortation to make a determined attempt.
